title: Lesson 1 Quiz: Coins, Tokens, and Digital Ownership

questions.text: What is the primary difference between a coin and a token?
options: A coin can only be used for payments, while a token can represent any asset.
A coin operates on its own independent blockchain, whereas a token is built on top of an existing blockchain and relies on that host network.
Tokens are always more valuable than coins because they are newer.
Coins require smart contracts to function, while tokens do not.
questions.explanation: A coin runs on its own independent blockchain network, while a token is built on top of an existing blockchain and relies entirely on the host network.

questions.text: Token transfers can be paid for using the tokens themselves.
questions.explanation: False. To transfer tokens you must still pay the network fee in the host network's native coin, never in the tokens themselves.
